claims.text: In a five-component high-entropy alloy outside strictly Nb-Ta- or Ti-based classes, superconducting properties are primarily governed by local chemical ordering of heavier 5d elements.
Heavier 5d elements create local structural distortions.
Local structural distortions around heavier 5d atoms enhance electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling caused by heavier 5d elements increases the superconducting critical temperature.
Higher-atomic-number species produce local changes in atomic coordination.
The starting material is a single-phase polycrystalline alloy containing at least five transition metals, each at or above 5 at%.
Heavier 5d transition metals will replace lighter 3d or 4d elements while all constituent concentrations remain at or above 5 at%.
High-temperature mixing followed by annealing promotes single-phase stability in the proposed alloy series.
Alloys containing heavier 5d constituents will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than otherwise similar lighter-element baselines.
The increase in superconducting transition temperature will be a few kelvins.
The lighter 3d- or 4d-element baseline has a lower superconducting transition temperature.
The proposed enhancement depends on retaining a single-phase high-entropy solid solution.
Secondary-phase formation may diminish or eliminate the predicted superconducting enhancement.
X-ray diffraction can be used to assess whether the compared samples are single phase.
A failure to observe a statistically significant increase in Tc would falsify the predicted 5d-induced superconducting enhancement.
Failure to detect local distortions would falsify the hypothesized role of 5d-induced local ordering.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule requires detection of local distortions or local ordering, but the listed measurements include no dedicated local-structure or chemical-ordering probe; conventional phase-purity XRD alone does not directly test the stated mediator.
